tests.name: each role's prompt and description are the Claude Code agent's, word for word
tests.why: reads the Claude Code agent files on disk against the role definitions; no host runs

tests.name: every role may ask the owner in the background: ask_user_async is not denied under the deny-all rule
tests.why: a unit check of the role permissions; no host runs

tests.name: --check passes on the written file and fails on a hand edit
tests.why: runs scripts/agents.ts on a scratch tree; no host runs

tests.name: pace: with no wakes to keep a latch, an over-limit pool refuses new agents with when it opens; under pace they run
tests.why: the fixture pool registers only `pace` over the world's RPC, as the real run's fake plugin does; the subagent tool and its children are the world's (host law: a subagent call starts a child session)

tests.name: codex pace: a subagent on a Codex-paced provider asks the Codex admission, with its model and role
tests.why: the admission is asked at the CodexAdmission port: its memory double records the model and the role the plugin asks with, where the real run read the script's `--model <m> --role <r>` args; the script's own argv is mods/orchestrate/codex/admission.ts's, covered by its unit test

tests.name: guard: an untyped subagent runs as the worker, `orchestrate-reviewer` as the verifier at medium effort
tests.why: the world's subagent tool, agent editor and per-agent tool permissions follow the fork's (host laws: subagent, agents, update); the call log is the memory double the plugin writes

tests.name: worker ceiling: under a root at max, the untyped worker runs at its model's default and the parent is told why; the verifier at medium
tests.why: a model asked with no variant is stored at `default`, as the fork's session create does (host law: subagent)

tests.name: compaction: on a 1M model, a planner session at 350k compacts at the 400k window; a worker session at 200k does not
tests.why: the world's automatic compaction keeps the fork's window and ceiling (host law: window) and runs the `compaction` hooks before the summary prompt (host law: compaction)

tests.name: units: an implementor's start and its hand-back move its unit in the run's log.md
tests.why: the unit's log.md is written by the skill's log.ts, a process the world does not run

tests.name: Sabbath: on Friday evening the subagent calls are refused with when work resumes, and no child starts
tests.why: the refusal is the plugin's tool.execute.before hook on the world's clock (host law: hooks)

tests.name: the held foreground call answers latched at once, and the parent goes on
tests.why: read off the TUI's frame: sim-tui's to move

tests.name: its row reads latched, with the hold and when it opens, and the dock counts it
tests.why: the worker's row and the dock, read off the TUI's frame: sim-tui's to move

tests.name: wake_list shows the latch: the subagent, its child, the hold and when it opens
tests.why: the wakes plugin's wake_list output on the world, read from the tool result where the real run read the request that carried it (the same text, JSON-escaped there)

tests.name: decided again while still held it latches again; once admitted it starts in the background on its child
tests.why: the scenario's stand-in pool on the world's RPC and clock; the wakes' latch re-decides on the world's timers (host laws: rpc, subagent)

tests.name: its answer wakes the parent, and its row reads done
tests.why: the done row, read off the TUI's frame: sim-tui's to move

tests.name: is steered once, after its planner ends and the owner's draft clears, and names its wait
tests.why: the nudges, the holds and the requests on the world: the running planner is the root's idle background (host law: idleBackground), the draft is the TUI's IDLE.draft report from a client of the world, the runs are the status script's table in the world's shell (the RunTables laws on both adapters), the wait is the queue's item over its RPC; the root's answer, the draft in the composer and the sidebar's wait stay real, read off the TUI's frames: sim-tui's to move

tests.name: the pool holds the first model, and the admission script is asked about the newest sol for the role
tests.why: the scenario's stand-in pool on the world's RPC; the admission is asked at the CodexAdmission port, whose memory double records the model and the role the plugin asks with, where the real run read the script's `--model <m> --role <r>` args (the argv is mods/orchestrate/codex/admission.ts's); the sols' family and release on the world's catalog (host law: catalog)

tests.name: it starts at once on sol, never latched, and the call log says why
tests.why: the call log is the memory double the plugin writes; the child's model as the world's subagent tool takes it (host law: subagent)

tests.name: the worker's request goes to sol
tests.why: the request's model is the child session's, as the world's provider receives it

tests.name: the parent reads where it ran and why, first in the call's result, then the answer, and its row shows sol
tests.why: the call's result and the completion notice in the parent's request on the world (host law: subagent); the parent's answer on screen and the planner's row stay real, read off the TUI's frame: sim-tui's to move
